newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Business boom slows in Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City.
newsitem.headline: Business boom slows in Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City.

text.p: The pace of foreign investment has slowed dramatically in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam's commercial hub, and economic growth in the metropolis has come off the boil, the Tuoi Tre newspaper said on Wednesday.

The paper quoted a source at the city's statistics department as saying that the value of foreign investment projects licensed in the first 11 months of this year was $971 million, a 52 percent drop from the same period of 1995.
Officials at the statistics department were not available to comment.

Tuoi Tre said the city, which has led the communist nation's reform-driven economic boom of recent years and taken over a third of foreign investment flows, was expected to see economic growth drop to 11.8 percent this year from 17.7 percent in 1995.
Industrial production growth was expected to fall one percentage point to 17.1 percent.
"Although the (industrial output) growth rate is high compared with that in the whole country, it is still slower than those of big cities such as Hanoi and Haiphong," the paper said.
It said industrial output growth for the whole country was expected to be 14 percent, but 19.3 percent in the capital of Hanoi and 20.3 percent in the northern port town of Haiphong.
